component.name: avro
component.title: Avro RPC
component.description: Call and expose Apache Avro RPC services over HTTP or Netty.
component.label: rpc

protocol.description: The Avro protocol (org.apache.avro.Protocol) that defines the messages, such as the PROTOCOL field of a class generated by the Avro compiler. Set this option or protocolClassName: the endpoint fails to start without a protocol.

protocolClassName.description: The fully qualified name of the class that defines the protocol. For a class generated by the Avro compiler, its static PROTOCOL field is used; for any other class or interface, Avro reflection builds the protocol and reflectionProtocol is turned on. Ignored when protocol is set.

protocolLocation.description: Not used: the component does not read this option. Use protocol or protocolClassName instead.

reflectionProtocol.description: Whether the protocol is a reflect protocol, built by Avro reflection from a Java interface, rather than one from classes generated by the Avro compiler. When true, the consumer and producer use the Avro reflect responder and requestor. Set it together with protocol: with protocolClassName it is turned on for a class without a PROTOCOL field.

singleParameter.description: Whether the consumer sets the message body to the one parameter of the called message, instead of an Object array of all parameters. The endpoint fails to start if the message, or any message of the protocol when messageName is not set, does not have exactly one parameter.

uriAuthority.description: The authority (host and port) of the endpoint URI, which the component sets from the URI. Consumers with the same authority share one Avro server, created with the protocol of the first consumer that starts. A value set on the component is replaced by the authority of the endpoint URI.

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

configuration.label: advanced
configuration.description: A shared configuration that every endpoint copies as its starting point. The options of the endpoint URI override its values.

serializablePackages.label: security
serializablePackages.description: Comma-separated list of additional packages that contain trusted Avro model classes. Avro 1.12+ validates classes resolved from schemas; Camel automatically trusts org.apache.avro for IPC and packages derived from the configured protocol. Use this option for any additional model packages not inferred from the protocol.

CamelAvroMessageName.description: The name of the protocol message to call. The producer reads it, and it takes precedence over the messageName of the endpoint. The consumer sets it to the name of the called message.

consumerOut.description: An Object array of the parameters of the called message, in the order of the protocol, with the message name in the CamelAvroMessageName header. With singleParameter the one parameter itself, such as a record

consumerReply.description: The response of the message, of its type in the protocol, such as the record class; it is not converted, so text or a Map fails for a record. Ignored for a message with a null response

producerIn.description: An Object array of the parameters of the message, in the order of the protocol, or the one parameter itself, such as a record. A java.util.List is not unpacked and a Map is not a record: build the parameter types of the protocol. The message name comes from the CamelAvroMessageName header, or else from the endpoint

producerOut.description: The response of the message, of its type in the protocol, such as the record class; no body for a message with a null response

transport.description: The transport: http or netty. With http, the consumer runs an Avro HTTP server on Jetty and the producer sends HTTP POST requests; with netty, both use the Avro Netty server and transceiver.

port.description: The port number. The consumer listens on it, and the producer connects to it.

host.description: The host name or IP address. The consumer binds its server to it, and the producer connects to it.

messageName.description: The name of the protocol message to call or serve. The producer calls it unless the CamelAvroMessageName header is set. A consumer with a message name serves only that message; a consumer without one serves every message that no other consumer on the same host and port serves.

exchangePattern.label: consumer,advanced
exchangePattern.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.
